messages:
Jared: FYI I'm seeing a new surge of tiny inference pods (0.125 GPU) in ap-southeast1b that end up Pending or Evicted. Alerts show 'too many of requested nic attachments' from scheduler. Started ~20m after the dense-packing scheduler ramp.
Mina: same. telemetry shows per-node attach ops spiked ~3x after dense pack. Likely saturating the attach-controller queue on a few racks.
Luis: can you paste a kubectl describe for one? curious whether it's scheduling or attach failing.
Jared: pasted one anonymized describe below:

```
Events:
  Type     Reason             Age   From               Message
  ----     ------             ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling   3m    default-scheduler  0/48 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu, 10 too many of requested nic attachments, 26 node(s) had untolerated taint.
  Normal   Scheduled          2m    default-scheduler  Successfully assigned default/tiny-infer-42 to rack-09-node-11
  Warning  FailedAttach      45s   kubelet            rpc error: code = DeadlineExceeded desc = Attach call timed out
  Normal   Evicted           10s   eviction-controller  NodeAffinity mismatch -> Evicted
```

Mina: Scheduled then FailedAttach -> attach system is the choke. Metrics show attach-controller pod CPU queue ~100% on racks 7-11 and attach duration median jumped from 120ms to 1.3s.
Luis: the scheduler dense-pack change increased preferSameRack=false for tiny pods to improve binpacking. That explains cross-rack attach ops growing.
Jared: ops proposal: 1) quick rollback of dense-pack flag in ap-southeast1 to stop new pressure 2) increase attach-controller replicas in the affected racks (or scale horizontally by node selector) 3) add an admission/scheduler predicate that checks nic-attach headroom before scheduling a tiny pod.
Mina: +1. Also add a short exponential backoff with jitter in the attach-controller (3 retries) and expose a readiness probe that reflects controller queue depth so scheduler can avoid racks with hot attachers.
Luis: I'll open the scheduler rollback canary and add the predicate PR. We should be careful: predicate should be soft at first (score rather than block) so we don't fragment GPU packing too hard.
buildbot: deploy-bot: scheduler/dense-pack-feature-flag rolled back in ap-southeast1 (deploy id: d-2026-0403-11). See https://ci.redwood/run/12577 :white_check_mark:
Mina: after rollback, attach latency dropped and PendingCount normalized in ~10m. Evictions reduced from ~6/min to ~0.6/min. Good immediate signal.
Jared: follow-ups: Luis -> scheduler predicate PR (score by nic_attach_headroom, soft penalty). Mina -> attach-controller retry+readiness PR and replica scaling experiment. I'll draft a runbook entry to check attach-controller queue and feature flag if tiny pods spike.
Luis: tagging capacity-team to investigate why some racks' attach-controller queue gets hot (host-level egress? single noisy VM?). Also capture per-node cgroup stats for the attach process.
Mina: note: long-term we should surface nic-attach ops as a first-class resource in node capacity (nic.attachable) so kube-scheduler can reason about it natively. For now soft-scoring is fastest.
Jared: agreed. I'll drop logs and graphs into the incident doc and link PRs here when ready. Leaving thread open for PR links and postmortem notes. :eyes:
